quirk_lead.text: Only production car ever built with gullwing doors on both sides
quirk_lead.note: Research lead only -- DISPROVEN by research. The Avantime did NOT have gullwing doors; it featured a double-kinematic parallel-opening hinge system. This inaccuracy drives the episode's corrective narrative.

claims.normalized_claim: The Renault Avantime did not have gullwing doors. It had two very long conventional doors with a double-kinematic parallel-opening hinge system that moved forward and out simultaneously to minimize outswing.

sources.title: Renault Avantime
sources.evidence_note: Describes the double-kinematic door system and clarifies the doors were not gullwing.

sources.title: Coupéspace: Driving the Renault Avantime
sources.evidence_note: Details the door mechanism and engineering solution for the long doors.

claims.safe_wording: The Avantime did not have gullwing doors; instead it used a double-kinematic hinge system on two unusually long conventional doors.
forbidden_or_unsupported_inference: That the Avantime had any gullwing door mechanism
claims.notes: This claim directly contradicts the episode's initial quirk premise. This is intentional and demonstrates the quirk-as-lead principle: research corrects the premise.

claims.normalized_claim: Thierry Métroz designed the Avantime's exterior under Patrick Le Quément's design direction. Métroz's stated goal was: 'We wanted someone walking around the car to be continually astonished.'

sources.title: Coupéspace: Driving the Renault Avantime
sources.evidence_note: Attributes the 'continually astonished' quote directly to Métroz.

claims.safe_wording: Thierry Métroz designed the exterior, saying the goal was to make people 'continually astonished' when viewing the car.

claims.normalized_claim: The Avantime's doors were 1.4 meters long to provide rear-seat access in a 2-door configuration. The double-kinematic hinge system solved the parking outswing problem by moving the door forward and out simultaneously.

sources.title: Renault Avantime
sources.evidence_note: Describes the double-kinematic hinge and its engineering purpose.

sources.title: Coupéspace: Driving the Renault Avantime
sources.evidence_note: Explains the 1.4-meter door length and the engineering solution for minimizing outswing.

claims.safe_wording: The Avantime's 1.4-meter doors gave rear-seat access, requiring an engineering solution to minimize outswing. The double-kinematic system moved the door forward and out simultaneously.

claims.normalized_claim: The Avantime was designed without B-pillars (the pillars between front and rear windows), creating a frameless glass effect from front to rear.

sources.title: Renault Avantime
sources.evidence_note: Describes the pillarless design and frameless window effect.

claims.safe_wording: The Avantime had no B-pillars, creating frameless glass from front to rear.

claims.normalized_claim: The Avantime's interior featured theater seating with elevated rear seats, a full panoramic sunroof with automatic opening, and aluminum space-frame construction.

sources.title: Renault Avantime
sources.evidence_note: Lists interior design features including theater seating, panoramic roof, and construction method.

claims.safe_wording: The interior featured elevated 'theater seating' in the rear, a full panoramic auto-opening roof, and aluminum space-frame construction.

claims.normalized_claim: 8,557 Renault Avantimes were produced across three model years (2001, 2002, 2003), making it one of the rarest 2000s-era production cars.

sources.title: Renault Avantime
sources.evidence_note: States 8,557 total units built across three production years.

claims.safe_wording: Just 8,557 Avantimes were built across the three model years.

claims.normalized_claim: First-year sales (2001) were 772 units; 2002 peaked at 5,037 units; production declined sharply in 2003 before ending in February.

sources.title: Renault Avantime Sales Figures
sources.evidence_note: Year-by-year breakdown of sales figures.

claims.safe_wording: Sales peaked in 2002 with 5,037 units; the first year saw only 772 sales, followed by sharp decline in 2003.

claims.normalized_claim: The Avantime was designed by Renault but manufactured by Matra at the Romorantin facility in France. Romorantin was originally built to produce the Renault Espace; when Renault moved Espace production in-house, Matra needed work, leading to the Avantime contract.

sources.title: Renault Avantime
sources.evidence_note: Details manufacturing partnership, Romorantin location, and historical context of the facility.

claims.safe_wording: Renault designed it, but Matra built every Avantime at its Romorantin plant—a facility originally built for Espace production that Renault had moved in-house.

claims.normalized_claim: Three engine options were offered: a 2.0-liter turbo gasoline (163 hp), a 2.2-liter turbo diesel (148 hp), and a 3.0-liter V6 gasoline (207 hp).

sources.title: RENAULT Avantime Specs, Performance & Photos - 2001, 2002, 2003
sources.evidence_note: Comprehensive engine specifications and performance data.

claims.safe_wording: Engine choices ranged from a 2.0-liter turbo (163 hp) and 2.2-liter diesel (148 hp) up to a 3.0-liter V6 (207 hp).

claims.normalized_claim: Renault and Matra initially targeted annual sales of 20,000 units per year.

sources.title: Renault Avantime: The Luxury MPV-Coupé That Was Too Strange to Survive
sources.evidence_note: Describes the original sales target and how far short actual sales fell.

claims.safe_wording: Renault and Matra initially hoped to sell 20,000 units annually.

claims.normalized_claim: Actual average sales were approximately 2,850 units per year (8,557 total ÷ 3 years), representing less than 15% of the original annual target of 20,000 units.
claims.safe_wording: Actual production averaged under 2,900 units annually—less than 15 percent of target.
claims.result: Actual average sales of ~2,850 units/year (14.26%) compared to 20,000 unit/year target

claims.normalized_claim: After Renault and Nissan formed their alliance in 1999, the companies considered a plan to sell an Infiniti-badged version of the Avantime in North America.

sources.title: America Almost Got the Wonderfully Quirky Renault Avantime
sources.evidence_note: Describes the Renault-Nissan alliance and the Infiniti-badged variant discussion.

claims.safe_wording: After forming their alliance in 1999, Renault and Nissan considered selling an Infiniti-badged version in North America.

claims.normalized_claim: The Infiniti Avantime plan was rejected. Renault and Nissan accountants calculated that converting the Avantime to meet US safety and emissions regulations would cost approximately $83.7 million, which both companies deemed unjustifiable given the car's limited market appeal.

sources.title: America Almost Got the Wonderfully Quirky Renault Avantime
sources.evidence_note: Reports the $83.7 million conversion cost estimate and the companies' rejection decision.

claims.safe_wording: The plan was rejected; converting the Avantime to US specifications was estimated to cost $83.7 million, which both companies deemed not worth the investment.
forbidden_or_unsupported_inference: That the cost was exactly $83.7M rather than an estimate

claims.normalized_claim: No Infiniti-badged Avantime was ever manufactured. The plan remained a strategic consideration only.

sources.title: America Almost Got the Wonderfully Quirky Renault Avantime
sources.evidence_note: Confirms no Infiniti version was actually built; plan was rejected before production.

claims.safe_wording: No Infiniti Avantime was ever actually built; the plan remained a road-not-taken decision.

claims.normalized_claim: The Renault Vel Satis (an upmarket sedan/MPV hybrid) launched in 2002, just one year into Avantime production. Both cars competed for Renault's luxury-car development budget and marketing attention.

sources.title: Rare Rides: The Absolutely Epic 2002 Renault Avantime, a Big Sales Flop
sources.evidence_note: Describes Vel Satis launch timing and market competition with the Avantime.

claims.safe_wording: In 2002, Renault launched the Vel Satis, another luxury vehicle that competed with the Avantime for Renault's marketing and development budget.

claims.normalized_claim: The Vel Satis was more commercially successful than the Avantime. Approximately 64,000 Vel Satis were produced worldwide versus 8,557 Avantimes.
claims.safe_wording: The Vel Satis outsold the Avantime decisively: roughly 64,000 produced worldwide versus just 8,557 Avantimes.
forbidden_or_unsupported_inference: That the Vel Satis was objectively better-designed
claims.notes: Derived from Vel Satis production (from compet01 source) and prod01_production_total.
claims.result: Vel Satis outsold Avantime by approximately 7.5 times

claims.normalized_claim: Matra, the Avantime's manufacturer, decided to exit automotive production in 2003. This decision was partly driven by financial losses incurred by poor Avantime sales.

sources.title: Renault Avantime
sources.evidence_note: States that Matra exited automotive production in 2003 partly due to Avantime losses.

claims.safe_wording: Matra, the car's builder, exited automotive production in 2003 partly because of losses from the Avantime's poor sales.

claims.normalized_claim: When Matra decided to exit, Renault chose to discontinue the Avantime rather than relocate production to one of Renault's own factories. The cost of restarting production elsewhere was deemed prohibitive.

sources.title: Renault Avantime
sources.evidence_note: Describes Renault's decision to discontinue rather than relocate production.

claims.safe_wording: Renault chose to discontinue the Avantime rather than move production to one of its own plants, judging the costs of retooling too high to justify.

claims.normalized_claim: The Avantime was marketed as a unique hybrid of sports coupe and family MPV (minivan). It was a 4-seat, 2-door vehicle with unusual proportions that blended high-performance styling with practical interior space.

sources.title: Renault Avantime
sources.evidence_note: Describes the coupe-MPV hybrid positioning and seating configuration.

claims.safe_wording: The Avantime was an unusual 4-seat, 2-door hybrid of sports coupe and family minivan—fast-looking but family-practical.

claims.normalized_claim: With only 8,557 units built, the Avantime is today one of the rarest 2000s-era production cars and is increasingly sought after by collectors interested in automotive design oddities and failures.

sources.title: Renault Avantime
sources.evidence_note: Notes the rarity status and collector interest in preserved examples.

claims.safe_wording: With only 8,557 built, the Avantime is now one of the rarest 2000s-era cars and increasingly sought by collectors.
